lessons.title: 状语从句的定义、本质与边界
lessons.meta: 从句整体给主句加上时间、原因、条件等关系
examples: When the bell rang, the students left.
Because the road was closed, we turned back.
The students left when the bell rang.
Because of the rain, we stayed inside.

analyses.label: 时间状语从句：when 连接从句与主句
原因状语从句：because 标出理由
介词短语作原因状语，不是从句

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 先看主干 the students left；When the bell rang 内部有 the bell＋rang，但整体只回答“学生什么时候离开”。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 主干是 we turned back；Because the road was closed 不占主语或宾语位置，而是说明“为什么返回”。

exampleNotes.title: 位置与标点
exampleNotes.body: 时间从句后置且与 left 紧密结合，通常不用逗号；英中文都可按“离开时间”理解，无需机械调序。

exampleNotes.title: 边界提醒
exampleNotes.body: Because of the rain 也表原因，但 the rain 没有谓语，所以它是介词短语；状语从句必须有自己的主谓骨架。

rules: 状语从句内部有自己的主谓骨架，外层则整体作状语，说明主句事件的时间、地点、原因等关系。
连接词不是只把两句话粘在一起；它要明确从句与主句之间的特定逻辑。
状语从句前置时通常用逗号与主句分隔；联系紧密的后置从句通常不用逗号。
判断是否为从句，要查它内部是否有主谓骨架；because of 等介词短语虽然也作状语，但不是从句。

questions.question: When the bell rang, the students left. 中 When 从句整体作什么？
questions.correct: 它内部有主谓，外层说明 left 的时间。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：它内部有主谓，外层说明 left 的时间。

questions.question: Because the road was closed, we turned back. 中 because 标出什么？
questions.correct: 道路关闭解释了为什么返回。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：道路关闭解释了为什么返回。

questions.question: The students left when the bell rang. 中紧密后置从句通常如何标点？
questions.correct: 后置时间从句与 left 紧密结合。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：后置时间从句与 left 紧密结合。

questions.question: Because of the rain 为什么不是状语从句？
questions.correct: the rain 是介词宾语，内部没有谓语。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：the rain 是介词宾语，内部没有谓语。

narration.text:
先看 When the bell rang, the students left。<#0.7#>真正要说的主干是 the students left，也就是“学生离开了”。When the bell rang 里面也有自己的主语 the bell 和动作 rang，但它整个放在主干旁边，只负责回答“什么时候离开”。这就是状语从句：里面是一套小句子，放到外面却像一个时间、原因或条件说明。
第二句 Because the road was closed, we turned back。主干换成 we turned back，前面的小句子回答“为什么返回”。所以连接词不能只当成开头标记；when 让两个事件形成时间关系，because 让它们形成原因关系，连接词一换，听者理解的关系也会跟着变。<#0.8#>
再看 The students left when the bell rang。时间从句放在后面，紧跟 left，通常不用逗号；放在前面时，逗号帮助我们看出背景讲完了，主句开始了。最后比较 Because of the rain, we stayed inside。the rain 只有名词，没有自己的谓语，因此 Because of the rain 是介词短语，不是从句。判断时先抓主句，再看附加部分有没有自己的主谓，最后问它给主句补的是哪一种关系。

lessons.title: 时间：when、while、as
lessons.meta: 时间点、持续过程与同步变化
examples: When the phone rang, I answered it.
While I was studying, my brother was sleeping.
As the sun rose, the sky grew brighter.

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: when 可引出某个时间点发生的事件。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: while 突出两个持续动作在一段时间内重叠。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: as 常表示两个过程同步发展。

rules: when 可用于时间点或时间段，适用范围最广。
while 常突出持续动作或状态的时间重叠。
as 常表示“随着”或两个动作同步发生、发展。

questions.question: ___ the phone rang, I answered it.
questions.correct: 时间点事件用 when。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：时间点事件用 when。

questions.question: ___ I was studying, my brother was sleeping.
questions.correct: 两个持续动作重叠，用 while。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：两个持续动作重叠，用 while。

questions.question: ___ the sun rose, the sky grew brighter. 强调同步变化。
questions.correct: as 可表示“随着”。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：as 可表示“随着”。

narration.text:
when、while 和 as 都能说“当……时”，但它们让我们看到的时间画面不一样。先看 When the phone rang, I answered it。<#0.7#>电话响是一个清楚的时间点，回答电话紧接着发生。这里用 when，重点是把 answered 定位在电话响起的那个时刻。when 的范围最宽，既能接时间点，也能接一段时间。
再看 While I was studying, my brother was sleeping。was studying 和 was sleeping 都在持续，两个动作有一段时间重叠。while 像是把一段时间框出来，让我们同时看到“我在学习”和“弟弟在睡觉”。如果只想抓某个突然发生的点，就不必强行用 while。<#0.8#>
最后看 As the sun rose, the sky grew brighter。太阳升起不是一下完成，天空变亮也在逐渐发生，两个变化一起往前走。as 在这里更接近“随着”。所以选择时不要只背中文翻译：要看画面。抓一个时刻，when 最自然；突出两个持续过程重叠，用 while；强调两个过程同步变化，用 as。先判断事件是一个点、一段重叠，还是一起发展，再选连接词。

lessons.title: 时间：before 与 after
lessons.meta: 明确事件先后关系
examples: Wash your hands before you eat.
After she finished the report, she sent it.
After she had finished the report, she sent it.

analyses.text: After she had finished the report,
analyses.label: 过去完成时 after 从句

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 主句动作发生在从句动作之前。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 从句事件先完成，主句事件随后发生。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: 先后已由 after 明确时，过去完成时可用于额外突出“先完成”，但并非总是必需。

rules: before 从句表示其事件晚于主句事件。
after 从句表示其事件早于主句事件。
before/after 已明确先后时，可根据强调和语境选择一般过去时或过去完成时。

questions.question: Wash your hands ___ you eat.
questions.correct: 洗手应先于吃饭。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：洗手应先于吃饭。

questions.question: ___ she finished the report, she sent it.
questions.correct: 完成报告后再发送。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：完成报告后再发送。

questions.question: After she ___ the report, she sent it. 哪项可突出先完成？
questions.correct: 过去完成时突出先于 sent。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：过去完成时突出先于 sent。

narration.text:
before 和 after 的核心不是翻译，而是给两个动作排队。先看 Wash your hands before you eat。<#0.7#>主句要求先洗手，before you eat 把“吃饭”放到后面，所以顺序是洗手在前，吃饭在后。看到 before 时，可以把从句里的动作当成一个时间界线，主句动作发生在这条界线之前。
第二句 After she finished the report, she sent it。after 从句放在前面，告诉我们报告先完成，随后才发送。不要因为从句写在句首，就误以为句首动作一定晚发生；真正决定先后的，是 after 的意义。<#0.8#>
再看 After she had finished the report, she sent it。had finished 用过去完成时，把“先完成”再突出一次。但 after 本身已经把顺序说清，所以很多语境里 finished 就足够，过去完成时不是见到 after 就必须使用。判断时先圈出两个事件，再让连接词排顺序：before 后的事件较晚，after 后的事件较早。时态负责补充强调，连接词才是判断时最先要看的路标。

lessons.title: 时间：until 与 since
lessons.meta: 截止点与起始点
examples: We waited until the bus arrived.
She did not leave until the meeting ended.
I have lived here since I graduated.

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: wait 延续到公交车到达这一截止点。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: not ... until 表示主句动作到截止点才开始。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: since 从句给出过去起点，主句常用现在完成时表示延续至今。

rules: 肯定句中，延续性动作可持续到 until 所引出的截止点。
not ... until 表示主句动作直到某一时间才发生。
since 时间从句表示起点；主句常用完成时，从句常用一般过去时。

questions.question: We waited ___ the bus arrived.
questions.correct: 等待持续到公交到达。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：等待持续到公交到达。

questions.question: She did not leave ___ the meeting ended.
questions.correct: not until 表示会议结束才离开。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：not until 表示会议结束才离开。

questions.question: I ___ here since I graduated.
questions.correct: 过去起点延续至今用现在完成时。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：过去起点延续至今用现在完成时。

narration.text:
until 和 since 都在时间线上找一个点，但一个看终点，一个看起点。先看 We waited until the bus arrived。<#0.7#>waited 是持续动作，等待一直延续，直到公交车到达才结束。until the bus arrived 就像给等待画出右边的终点，重点不是公交到达持续多久，而是等待到哪里停止。
第二句 She did not leave until the meeting ended。这里不能机械理解成“离开一直持续”。did not leave 表示之前始终没有离开，会议结束时，leave 这个动作才发生。not ... until 常表达“直到……才……”。<#0.8#>
再看 I have lived here since I graduated。since I graduated 给出过去的起点，have lived 表示从毕业以后一直延续到现在。于是常见组合是：since 从句用一般过去时交代起点，主句用现在完成时连接过去和现在。判断时先问动作是在某一点结束，还是从某一点开始。看到终点用 until；看到起点并延续到现在，用 since 和完成时。特别注意 not until，它说的是动作到终点才开始，不是普通的“持续到”。

lessons.title: 时间：as soon as 与 once
lessons.meta: 紧接发生与条件一旦成立
examples: Call me as soon as you arrive.
Once you understand the rule, the task becomes easier.
I will tell you as soon as I know.

analyses.label: as soon as 时间从句
将来时间从句用一般现在时

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 从句事件一发生，主句动作紧接着发生。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: once 表示“一旦”，兼有时间先后和条件成立意味。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: 主句用 will，从句表达将来但用一般现在时 know。

rules: as soon as 表示一个事件发生后另一个事件立即发生。
once 表示“一旦”，常兼有时间和条件色彩。
谈将来时，as soon as/once 从句通常用一般现在时，不用 will 表单纯将来。

questions.question: Call me ___ you arrive.
questions.correct: 表示一到就打电话。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：表示一到就打电话。

questions.question: ___ you understand the rule, the task becomes easier.
questions.correct: once 表示“一旦”。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：once 表示“一旦”。

questions.question: I will tell you as soon as I ___.
questions.correct: 将来时间从句用一般现在时。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：将来时间从句用一般现在时。

narration.text:
as soon as 和 once 都把两个事件接得很近，但重点略有不同。先看 Call me as soon as you arrive。<#0.7#>arrive 一发生，call 就要紧接着发生，中间不希望有明显等待。as soon as 强调“一……就……”，适合表达立即跟上的动作。
第二句 Once you understand the rule, the task becomes easier。这里 once 不只是说时间先后，还带有“条件一旦成立”的感觉：只要理解规则，任务就会变容易。所以 once 经常站在时间和条件的交界处。<#0.8#>
最后看 I will tell you as soon as I know。主句 will tell 明确指向将来，从句虽然也说将来的“知道”，却用一般现在时 know，不说 will know。原因是这个连接语已经把它放进未来时间安排里，不需要再用普通 will 重复标记。判断时先看你要表达的是“马上跟着发生”，还是“一旦条件成立”。前者使用表示“一……就……”的连接语，后者可用 once。谈将来时，再检查从句是否误加了 will。

lessons.title: 地点：where 与 wherever
lessons.meta: 在……的地方与无论哪里
examples: Stay where you are.
Where there is water, life can exist.
Wherever you go, I will follow you.

exampleNotes.title: 语序翻译
exampleNotes.body: where you are 表示“在你所在的地方”，整体修饰 stay。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 从句概括“有水的地方”。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: wherever 表示“无论去哪里”，范围不限。

rules: where 地点状语从句整体说明主句动作发生的位置。
句首 where 从句可概括“在……的地方”，后接主句结果。
wherever 表示任意地点或“无论哪里”，语义范围比 where 更开放。

questions.question: Stay ___ you are.
questions.correct: 从句说明 stay 的地点。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：从句说明 stay 的地点。

questions.question: ___ there is water, life can exist.
questions.correct: 表示“有水的地方”。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：表示“有水的地方”。

questions.question: ___ you go, I will follow you.
questions.correct: 表示无论去哪里。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：表示无论去哪里。

narration.text:
地点状语从句不是单独说一个地点名，而是用一整套主谓关系回答“在哪里”。先看 Stay where you are。<#0.7#>主干只有 Stay，也就是“待着”。where you are 里面有 you 和 are，整个小句子说明 stay 的地点：待在你现在所在的位置。它不是 stay 的宾语，而是给动作补地点范围。
再看 Where there is water, life can exist。where there is water 概括的不是某一个已知地点，而是所有“有水的地方”；主句说这些地方可能有生命。句首地点从句先搭好一个空间背景，后面的结论在这个范围内成立。<#0.8#>
最后看 Wherever you go, I will follow you。wherever 比 where 更开放，意思是无论你去哪个地方，主句结果都不改变。选择时先问范围是否有限：只是指出动作发生的地方，用 where；想把所有可能地点都包括进去，用 wherever。判断地点从句时仍要检查内部主谓；这三个地点从句都有自己的主语和谓语，有了这套骨架，它才是从句，而不只是一个地点词。

lessons.title: 原因：because、since、as
lessons.meta: 直接原因与已知背景
examples: We stayed inside because it was raining.
Since everyone is here, we can begin.
As it was getting late, we went home.

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: because 直接回答为什么，原因焦点较强。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: since 常把双方已知或容易接受的原因作为背景。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: as 原因从句常前置，原因语气较弱、偏背景。

rules: because 表达直接、重点原因，最自然地回答 why。
since 表原因时常表示对方已知、显然或作为推理前提的背景。
as 表原因时语气通常较弱，常用于句首提供背景。

questions.question: Why did you stay inside? — ___ it was raining.
questions.correct: 直接回答 why 使用 because。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：直接回答 why 使用 because。

questions.question: ___ everyone is here, we can begin. 表示已知前提。
questions.correct: since 可提供已知原因背景。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：since 可提供已知原因背景。

questions.question: ___ it was getting late, we went home. 表示背景原因。
questions.correct: as 可弱化原因并前置。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：as 可弱化原因并前置。

narration.text:
because、since 和 as 都能给原因，但说话人把原因放在多重要的位置，并不一样。先看 We stayed inside because it was raining。<#0.7#>如果别人问“为什么待在里面”，because it was raining 就是直接答案。because 把下雨作为重点原因，解释力度最清楚。
第二句 Since everyone is here, we can begin。everyone is here 更像双方都看得到、都能接受的前提。说话人不是重点追问原因，而是借这个已知背景推出“可以开始”。since 在这里接近“既然”。<#0.8#>
再看 As it was getting late, we went home。天色渐晚被轻轻放在句首当背景，真正要推进的信息是 we went home。as 表原因时通常比 because 弱，也常前置。选择时不要把三个词当成随意替换：需要正面回答 why，用 because；原因已经明显，拿来作为推理前提，用 since；只是顺带铺一个较弱背景，可用 as。先判断原因是不是句子的焦点，再决定连接词。

lessons.title: 目的：so that 与 in order that
lessons.meta: 为了让某事能够发生
examples: Speak slowly so that everyone can understand.
She left early so that she could catch the bus.
In order that no one would notice, he entered quietly.
He spoke so quietly that nobody heard him.

analyses.text: so that she could catch the bus.
analyses.label: 过去语境目的从句

analyses.text: In order that no one would notice,
analyses.label: 正式目的状语从句

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 从句说明慢慢说的目的，常含 can/may。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: 过去语境常用 could/might/would 表示预期目的。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: in order that 较正式，常用于明确目的并可前置。

exampleNotes.title: 易混辨析
exampleNotes.body: 这里是 so＋副词 quietly＋that，说明“实际导致无人听见”，不是 so that 直接引出的意图。

rules: so that 引导目的从句时常与 can/could、may/might、will/would 等情态形式搭配。
主句为过去语境时，目的从句常使用 could、might 或 would。
in order that 比 so that 更正式、更明确地标示目的，并可前置。
so that 目的从句说意图；so＋形容词/副词＋that 结果从句说某程度实际导致什么。

questions.question: Speak slowly ___ everyone can understand.
questions.correct: 从句说明说慢的目的。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：从句说明说慢的目的。

questions.question: She left early so that she ___ catch the bus.
questions.correct: 过去语境使用 could。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：过去语境使用 could。

questions.question: 哪一连接词更正式地表示目的？
questions.correct: in order that 是正式目的连接语。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：in order that 是正式目的连接语。

questions.question: He spoke so quietly that nobody heard him. 中 that 从句表什么？
questions.correct: so quietly 的程度导致了该结果。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：so quietly 的程度导致了该结果。

narration.text:
目的从句说的是“做这件事，想让什么发生”，它描述意图，不保证结果真的实现。先看 Speak slowly so that everyone can understand。<#0.7#>主干是 Speak slowly，慢慢说的目标，是让每个人能够听懂。can understand 表示这种能力或可能性，因此 so that 后常见 can、may 一类情态词。
第二句 She left early so that she could catch the bus。主句在过去，目的从句用 could，表示她早走是为了能赶上公交。句子只交代她的打算，并没有保证最后一定赶上。in order that no one would notice, he entered quietly 也是目的，但 in order that 更正式，放在句首时，目的被先交代出来。<#0.8#>
最后比较 He spoke so quietly that nobody heard him。这里不是“为了没人听见”，而是声音安静到实际造成没人听见。结构是 so quietly 加 that，quietly 的程度带来结果。判断目的还是结果，可以问：这是行动前想达到的目标，还是行动后已经出现的后果？目标用普通或更正式的目的连接结构；程度造成的实际后果，用 so 加形容词或副词再接 that。

lessons.title: 结果：so...that 与 such...that
lessons.meta: 程度达到某种结果
examples: The box was so heavy that I could not lift it.
It was such a difficult question that nobody answered it.
There were so many people that we could not enter.

analyses.text: that I could not lift it.
analyses.label: 结果状语从句

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: so 修饰形容词 heavy，that 从句说明结果。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: such 修饰“a＋形容词＋名词”短语。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: many/much/few/little 前通常用 so。

rules: so + 形容词/副词 + that 表示程度导致的结果。
such + (a/an) + 形容词 + 名词 + that 表示某类事物造成的结果。
many、much、few、little 表数量时通常使用 so ... that。

questions.question: The box was ___ heavy that I could not lift it.
questions.correct: heavy 是形容词，使用 so。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：heavy 是形容词，使用 so。

questions.question: It was ___ difficult question that nobody answered it.
questions.correct: 名词短语使用 such a。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：名词短语使用 such a。

questions.question: There were ___ many people that we could not enter.
questions.correct: many 前用 so。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：many 前用 so。

narration.text:
so...that 和 such...that 都在说“程度达到这里，于是出现那个结果”。区别先看 that 前面中心是什么。The box was so heavy that I could not lift it。<#0.7#>heavy 是形容词，so 直接把“重”的程度提高，that 从句说明实际结果：我抬不起来。结构可以先抓成 so heavy，再接结果。
第二句 It was such a difficult question that nobody answered it。这里中心是 question，是名词。such 带着整个 a difficult question，表示“这样一道难题”，随后出现无人回答的结果。不是看到 difficult 就只选 so，还要看它和 a、question 组成了完整名词短语。<#0.8#>
再看 There were so many people that we could not enter。many 虽然修饰 people，但 many、much、few、little 表数量时习惯放在 so 后面，所以是 so many people。选择时先看结构：形容词或副词直接表示程度，用 so；a 加形容词加名词这一整组，用 such；遇到数量词 many、much、few、little，优先用 so。that 后面说的都是真实造成的结果，不是行动目的。

lessons.title: 条件：if
lessons.meta: 真实可能、假设条件与命令建议
examples: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.
If you heat ice, it melts.
If you need help, call me.

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: 将来真实条件从句用一般现在时 rains，主句可用 will。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 普遍事实常用“if＋一般现在时，主句一般现在时”。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 主句可用祈使句表达条件成立后的指令。

rules: 真实条件 if 从句提出可能成立的条件，主句说明结果。
普遍规律可用 if 加一般现在时，主句也用一般现在时。
条件句主句不只可用 will，也可使用情态动词或祈使句。

questions.question: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay home.
questions.correct: 将来条件从句用一般现在时。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：将来条件从句用一般现在时。

questions.question: If you heat ice, it ___.
questions.correct: 普遍事实两边可用一般现在时。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：普遍事实两边可用一般现在时。

questions.question: If you need help, ___ me.
questions.correct: 主句可用祈使句。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：主句可用祈使句。

narration.text:
if 从句先提出一个前提，主句再说这个前提成立会怎样。先看 If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home。<#0.7#>下雨还没有发生，只是明天可能出现的条件。主句用 will stay 说结果，从句却用 rains，不用 will rain。一般现在时放在这里不表示“现在下雨”，而是英语表达将来条件的常见方式。
第二句 If you heat ice, it melts。这里不是预测某一次未来，而是在说反复成立的规律：只要给冰加热，它就融化。因此条件和结果都用一般现在时。<#0.8#>
再看 If you need help, call me。条件成立后，主句不是 will，而是祈使句 call me，直接给出建议或指令。这说明条件句的主句有多种样子，不必套成唯一公式。判断时分两步：先看条件是未来可能、普遍规律，还是给指令的前提；再选主句形式。未来真实条件常见“if 加一般现在时，主句用 will”；规律两边都用现在时；建议和命令可以直接用祈使句。

lessons.title: 条件：unless、as long as、provided that
lessons.meta: 除非、只要与前提条件
examples: Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
You may stay as long as you are quiet.
We will go provided that the weather is safe.

analyses.text: as long as you are quiet.
analyses.label: as long as 条件从句

analyses.text: provided that the weather is safe.
analyses.label: provided that 条件从句

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: unless 相当于 if ... not；从句通常不再重复 not。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: as long as 表示“只要”某条件持续满足。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: provided/providing that 明确表示“前提是”。

rules: unless 表示 if ... not；除特殊语义外，通常不与 not 重复。
as long as 表条件时表示“只要”，不要与表示时间长度的本义混淆。
provided/providing that 表示明确前提，语气较正式。

questions.question: ___ you hurry, you will miss the bus.
questions.correct: unless 表示 if you do not hurry。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：unless 表示 if you do not hurry。

questions.question: You may stay ___ you are quiet.
questions.correct: 表示“只要保持安静”。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：表示“只要保持安静”。

questions.question: We will go ___ the weather is safe.
questions.correct: provided that 表明确条件。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：provided that 表明确条件。

narration.text:
三种连接方式都在设条件，但门槛的方向不同。先看 Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus。<#0.7#>unless you hurry 相当于“如果你不赶快”，也就是“不赶快的话”。unless 自己已经带有否定方向，通常不要再重复否定，否则意思可能变乱。
第二句 You may stay as long as you are quiet。这里 as long as 不是“和……一样长”，而是“只要”。安静这个条件持续满足，就可以留下。它强调许可建立在这个条件上。<#0.8#>
再看 We will go provided that the weather is safe。provided that 把前提说得很明确：只有天气安全，才会去，语气比普通 if 更正式。选择时先看你想怎样设门槛：第一种表达“如果不……就……”；第二种表达“只要条件保持成立”；第三种正式说明“前提是”。最后再检查第一种连接词后面是否不必要地重复了否定。

lessons.title: 让步：although、though、even though
lessons.meta: 尽管条件存在，主句结果仍成立
examples: Although it was cold, we went out.
Though he was tired, he kept working.
Even though she knew the risk, she continued.
Even if it rains, we will go.

analyses.text: Even though she knew the risk,
analyses.label: even though 强让步从句
even if 假设让步从句

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 寒冷本应阻碍外出，但主句结果仍发生。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: though 通常比 although 稍口语，基本意义相近。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: even though 强调让步事实出乎预期。

exampleNotes.title: 易混辨析
exampleNotes.body: even if 把下雨当作尚未确定的情况；even though it is raining 则把下雨当作事实。

rules: although 引导事实性让步，表示主句结果与通常预期相反。
though 与 although 基本意义相近，though 常更口语、位置更灵活。
even though 强调“即使事实如此仍然”，让步力度更强。
even though 引出已知事实，even if 引出假设或尚未确定的情况。

questions.question: ___ it was cold, we went out.
questions.correct: 前后是让步关系。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：前后是让步关系。

questions.question: 哪一词通常比 although 稍口语？
questions.correct: though 基本意义相同但更口语。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：though 基本意义相同但更口语。

questions.question: 哪一项让步强调更强？
questions.correct: even 增强出乎预期的对比。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：even 增强出乎预期的对比。

questions.question: 下雨尚未确定，但无论如何都去：___ it rains, we will go.
questions.correct: 未确定的假设用 even if。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：未确定的假设用 even if。

narration.text:
让步关系可以理解成：前面的情况本来可能阻止结果，可结果还是发生了。先看 Although it was cold, we went out。<#0.7#>天冷通常让人不想外出，但 we went out 仍然成立。although 不是原因，它专门提醒听者：后面的结果和通常预期不一样。
Though he was tired, he kept working 表达同样的转折预期，though 一般更口语、更灵活。Even though she knew the risk, she continued 里的 even 把阻碍再加强：她明明知道风险，仍然继续，反差更明显。<#0.8#>
最后看 Even if it rains, we will go。这里下雨还没确定，只是假设一个可能情况；无论是否发生，去这件事都不变。even though 引出的是已经承认的事实，even if 引出的是尚未确定的假设。判断时先找“本来会阻止什么”的因素，再看它是事实还是可能。普通事实让步用 although 或 though；想加强反差用 even though；情况尚未发生，只是假设也不改变结果，用 even if。

lessons.title: 将来时间和条件从句不用普通 will
lessons.meta: 主将从现及其准确边界
examples: When she arrives, we will start.
If he calls, tell me.
Once you have finished, you may leave.
I do not know whether he will come.
If you will wait here, I will check the schedule.

analyses.label: 将来时间从句用一般现在时
将来条件从句用一般现在时
将来从句用现在完成时
if 条件从句：will 表意愿

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: arrives 表将来时间，但从句不用 will arrive。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: if 从句表达未来可能条件，用 calls。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: 现在完成时可突出从句动作先完成，再发生主句动作。

exampleNotes.title: 边界提醒
exampleNotes.body: 这里 whether 引导宾语从句，不是条件状语从句，因此可用 will；不要把规则扩大到所有含 if/whether 的从句。

exampleNotes.title: 边界提醒
exampleNotes.body: 从句里的 will 不是单纯预测将来，而是“如果你愿意等”；因此“条件从句不用 will”不是无例外口诀。

rules: when、before、after、until、as soon as 等将来时间从句通常用一般现在时表达将来。
真实将来条件 if/unless/as long as 从句通常用一般现在时表达将来。
现在完成时可在将来时间或条件从句中突出动作完成。
“主将从现”只适用于相应时间/条件状语从句，不适用于所有宾语从句。
if 从句中的 will 若表示意愿、坚持或客气请求，而非单纯将来，可以使用。

questions.question: When she ___, we will start.
questions.correct: 将来时间从句用一般现在时。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：将来时间从句用一般现在时。

questions.question: If he ___, tell me.
questions.correct: 将来条件从句用一般现在时。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：将来条件从句用一般现在时。

questions.question: Once you ___, you may leave. 强调先完成。
questions.correct: 现在完成时额外突出从句动作已完成。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：现在完成时额外突出从句动作已完成。

questions.question: I do not know whether he ___ come.
questions.correct: 当前语境转述未来可使用 will。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：当前语境转述未来可使用 will。

questions.question: If you ___ wait here, I will check the schedule. 表“如果你愿意”。
questions.correct: will 在此表意愿，不是单纯将来。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：will 在此表意愿，不是单纯将来。

narration.text:
“主将从现”不是看到两个分句就套用，而是专门处理将来的时间或真实条件。先看 When she arrives, we will start。<#0.7#>开始发生在将来，主句用 will start；when 已经把 arrives 放到未来时间里，所以从句用一般现在时。If he calls, tell me 也一样，calls 表示将来可能条件，主句则直接用祈使句。
Once you have finished, you may leave 使用现在完成时 have finished，重点是先把事情完成，再允许离开。它仍属于现在形式，不需要普通 will。<#0.8#>
但 I do not know whether he will come 不受这条规则限制，因为 whether he will come 是 do not know 的宾语，讨论的是“他是否会来”，不是条件状语从句，所以可以用 will。最后看 If you will wait here, I will check the schedule。从句里的 will 表“如果你愿意等”，说的是意愿，不是单纯预测。判断时先确认从句功能：是将来时间或真实条件，通常用现在形式；是宾语从句，或者 will 自己表达意愿，就不能机械删掉。

lessons.title: because–so 与 although–but 的边界
lessons.meta: 英语从属连词与主句连接不重复
examples: Because it rained, we stayed home.
It rained, so we stayed home.
Although she was tired, she continued.

exampleNotes.title: 边界提醒
exampleNotes.body: 标准句中 because 已连接原因从句，主句前不再加 so。

exampleNotes.title: 易混辨析
exampleNotes.body: 也可用 so 连接两个分句，但此时不用 because。

exampleNotes.title: 边界提醒
exampleNotes.body: although 已表达让步，标准结构中主句前不再加 but。

rules: 标准英语通常不用 because ... so ... 同时连接同一组原因和结果分句。
可选择 because 从属结构，或选择 so 并列结果结构，视信息重点而定。
标准英语通常不用 although/though ... but ... 同时连接同一让步关系。

questions.question: Because it rained, ___ we stayed home.
questions.correct: because 已建立原因关系。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：because 已建立原因关系。

questions.question: It rained, ___ we stayed home.
questions.correct: 前句是原因，后句是结果，用 so 并列。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：前句是原因，后句是结果，用 so 并列。

questions.question: Although she was tired, ___ she continued.
questions.correct: although 已表达让步。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：although 已表达让步。

narration.text:
中文里常说“因为……所以……”“虽然……但是……”，英语标准句子通常只选一套连接方式。先看 Because it rained, we stayed home。<#0.7#>because 已经把 it rained 变成原因背景，后面的 we stayed home 是主句，中间不需要再加 so。不是少翻了“所以”，而是英语已经用 because 把关系交代完成。
第二句 It rained, so we stayed home 也正确，但结构变了。这里没有 because，so 把“下雨”和“待在家”两个分句并列起来，明确后一句是结果。你可以突出原因从属关系，也可以用 so 推出结果，但不要两边同时占用。<#0.8#>
Although she was tired, she continued 同样如此。although 已经表示“疲惫本应阻碍继续，但结果仍发生”，主句前不再加 but。判断时先圈出已有连接词：用了 because，就直接接主句；用了 although 或 though，也直接接主句。想用 so 或 but，就拿掉前面的从属连词，重新组织成并列分句。英语不是漏掉一半，而是每个关系只让一套结构负责。

groups.title: 进阶挑战 · 6 节
groups.copy: 细微意义、比较方式、省略转换和综合边界。

lessons.title: 让步：while、no matter 与 wh-ever
lessons.meta: 对比让步与无条件让步
examples: While I understand your point, I disagree.
No matter what happens, stay calm.
Wherever she goes, she makes friends.
Whoever calls, do not answer

analyses.label: no matter what 让步从句

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: while 表“虽然/尽管”时突出两种看法的对比。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 表示无论发生什么，主句都成立。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: wherever 相当于 no matter where，在此表达无条件让步。

exampleNotes.title: 边界提醒
exampleNotes.body: wh-ever 在此作让步状语；no matter + wh- 不能替代名词性主宾语功能，本课不展开名词性用法。

rules: while 可表示对比性让步，通常位于句首，意为“虽然”。
no matter + wh- 表示无论哪种情况，主句结论均不改变。
wh-ever 可相当于 no matter + wh- 引导让步状语从句。
判断 wh-ever 时必须看整体功能；本课只处理其状语让步用法。

questions.question: ___ I understand your point, I disagree. 表对比让步。
questions.correct: while 可表示“虽然”。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：while 可表示“虽然”。

questions.question: ___ what happens, stay calm.
questions.correct: no matter what 表无条件让步。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：no matter what 表无条件让步。

questions.question: Wherever she goes 最接近什么？
questions.correct: wherever 可等于 no matter where。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：wherever 可等于 no matter where。

questions.question: 判断 wh-ever 从句类型应先看什么？
questions.correct: 相同形式可承担不同从句功能。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：相同形式可承担不同从句功能。

narration.text:
这一节的让步不是简单说“但是”，而是说明无论出现哪一种情况，主句结论仍然不变。先看 While I understand your point, I disagree。<#0.7#>我理解你的观点，却仍不同意。while 在这里不表示两个动作同时发生，而是把“理解”和“不同意”放在一起形成对比，接近“虽然”。
No matter what happens, stay calm 把可能发生的所有事情都包括进来：不管发生什么，保持冷静这条指令不变。Wherever she goes, she makes friends 也是同样思路，wherever 表示“无论哪里”，不论地点怎样变化，结果都成立。<#0.8#>
最后看 Whoever calls, do not answer。不论打来电话的是谁，指令都不改变。判断 wh-ever 时不能只看到 ever 就下结论，要看整块内容在句中做什么。这些从句都给主句加“无论哪种情况”的让步范围。选择时，对比两个立场可用 while；想展开所有可能，用 no matter 加疑问词，或用 whatever、wherever、whoever 这样的形式。

lessons.title: 比较：than 与 as...as
lessons.meta: 比较级差异与同等比较
examples: Mia runs faster than I do.
This room is as bright as that one is.
She is taller than me / than I am.

analyses.label: 比较基准：than me 为短语，than I am 为从句

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: than I do 只提供 faster 的比较基准；do 代替 runs，避免重复完整谓语。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: bright 是 room 的表语；第二个 as 引出 that one is 作同等比较的基准。

exampleNotes.title: 易混辨析
exampleNotes.body: than me 在日常英语常见；than I am 明示主语和谓语，是完整比较从句，更正式。

rules: than 引导比较基准，从句中重复成分常用助动词替代或省略。
as + 形容词/副词 + as 表示同等程度，第二个 as 可引出比较从句。
than 后代词在实际英语中有宾格短语和完整主格从句两种常见形式，正式度不同。

questions.question: Mia runs faster than I ___.
questions.correct: do 替代 runs。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：do 替代 runs。

questions.question: This room is ___ bright ___ that one is.
questions.correct: 同等比较使用 as ... as。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：同等比较使用 as ... as。

questions.question: 哪一项更明确地显示完整比较从句？
questions.correct: than I am 明示主语和谓语。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：than I am 明示主语和谓语。

narration.text:
比较从句的任务，是给比较词提供一个基准。先看 Mia runs faster than I do。<#0.7#>主干先说 Mia runs faster，但 faster 必须回答“比谁更快”。than I do 提供参照，do 代替前面已经出现的 runs，避免把相同的“跑”再完整说一遍。这个 do 不是新的动作意思，只是把相同谓语简洁地接住。
第二句 This room is as bright as that one is。第一个 as 和 bright 组成 as bright，表示达到同等亮度；第二个 as 引出比较对象 that one。后面的 is 对应前面的 is bright，重复的 bright 可以省掉。<#0.8#>
再看 She is taller than me / than I am。than me 在日常口语中很常见，可以看成较短的比较短语；than I am 明确写出主语和谓语，是完整比较从句，也更正式。判断时先找比较中心，是 faster、taller，还是 as bright；再找它跟谁比。比较从句里与前面重复的内容常被助动词代替或直接省略，所以不要因为句子短，就误认为结构不完整。

lessons.title: 方式：as 与 as if/as though
lessons.meta: 按照某方式与仿佛情形
examples: Do as I showed you.
He speaks as if he knows everything.
He talks as if he knew everything.

analyses.label: 虚拟色彩的 as if 从句

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: as 表示“按照……的方式”。

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 一般现在时可表示说话者认为这种可能性真实或开放。

exampleNotes.title: 易混辨析
exampleNotes.body: 过去式 knew 可表达与当前事实距离较远或说话者不相信。

rules: as 引导方式从句，表示“按照……的样子/方式”。
as if/as though 后可用普通陈述时态，表示看起来可能真实。
as if/as though 后用过去式或 were 可表达与当前事实相反或距离感。

questions.question: Do ___ I showed you.
questions.correct: as 表示按所示方式。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：as 表示按所示方式。

questions.question: 看起来可能真实时，as if 后可用什么？
questions.correct: 真实可能使用普通时态。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：真实可能使用普通时态。

questions.question: He talks as if he ___ everything. 表示说话者不相信。
questions.correct: 过去式表达距离或非真实。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：过去式表达距离或非真实。

narration.text:
方式从句回答“动作是按照什么样子发生的”。先看 Do as I showed you。<#0.7#>主句只有 Do，真正的操作方式由 as I showed you 补出来，意思是按照我展示的方法做。as 在这里不是原因，也不是时间，要看它是否给动作提供一个可照着执行的样子。
第二句 He speaks as if he knows everything。说话的样子像是他什么都知道。knows 用一般现在时，说明说话人至少把这种可能性留着，并没有明确断定它不真实。<#0.8#>
再看 He talks as if he knew everything。同样是“仿佛”，knew 用过去式却不一定表示过去时间，它可以把情况推远，暗示说话人并不相信他真的什么都知道。选择时先分两类：明确表示“按照……方式”，用 as；表示外在样子“好像……”，用 as if 或 as though。然后再判断说话人态度：觉得可能真实，用普通时态；想表达与现实有距离或不相信，可用过去式，涉及 be 时也常见 were。

lessons.title: 时间从句的时态关系
lessons.meta: 同时、打断、先后与延续
examples: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
When I arrived, they were eating.
By the time we arrived, the film had started.

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: 持续背景用过去进行时，短暂打断事件用一般过去时。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: arrived 是时间点，were eating 是当时正在进行。

exampleNotes.title: 时态观察
exampleNotes.body: 电影开始早于到达，用过去完成时突出先发生。

rules: 持续背景动作常用过去进行时，打断它的短暂动作常用一般过去时。
when 可定位一个时间点，与主句进行时搭配表达“当时正在”。
by the time 强调截止点，较早完成的过去动作常用过去完成时。

questions.question: While I ___, the phone rang.
questions.correct: 持续背景用过去进行时。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：持续背景用过去进行时。

questions.question: When I arrived, they ___.
questions.correct: 表示到达时正在吃。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：表示到达时正在吃。

questions.question: By the time we arrived, the film ___.
questions.correct: 过去完成时额外突出电影开始早于到达。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：过去完成时额外突出电影开始早于到达。

narration.text:
时间从句里的时态，是在帮我们看清两个过去动作怎样摆放：谁在持续，谁突然发生，谁更早完成。先看 While I was cooking, the phone rang。<#0.7#>was cooking 拉出一段持续背景，rang 是在这段背景中突然出现的短动作。可以想成一条长线被一个点打断，所以背景用过去进行时，点状事件用一般过去时。
第二句 When I arrived, they were eating。arrived 是到达的时间点，were eating 表示在那个时刻，吃饭正在进行。它和第一句的画面方向相反：时间点放在从句，持续背景放在主句，但判断方法相同。<#0.8#>
再看 By the time we arrived, the film had started。到达是截止点，电影开始发生得更早。had started 用过去完成时把“早于另一个过去动作”标出来。选择时不要只看到 while 就一定用进行时，而要看动作本身是否持续；也不要见到两个过去动作就都用过去完成时。先画时间线：持续背景用过去进行时，短动作常用一般过去时，需要突出在另一个过去点之前已经完成，才用过去完成时。

lessons.title: 状语从句的省略与分词转换
lessons.meta: 主语一致、be 省略与主动被动关系
examples: When (she was) young, she lived abroad.
If necessary, call me.
Walking home, I met Mia.
Although invited, he did not attend.

analyses.label: 省略主语和 be 的时间从句
现在分词作时间或伴随状语

exampleNotes.title: 结构转换
exampleNotes.body: 从句主语与主句主语相同且谓语含 be 时，可省略从句主语和 be。

exampleNotes.title: 结构转换
exampleNotes.body: If necessary 相当于 If it is necessary，是固定简洁表达。

exampleNotes.title: 结构转换
exampleNotes.body: 可对应 While I was walking home；逻辑主语必须是 I。

exampleNotes.title: 结构转换
exampleNotes.body: he 承受 invite，保留 although 可明确让步关系。

rules: 当状语从句主语与主句主语一致且从句含 be 时，常可省略从句主语和 be。
if necessary/possible 等是常见的“连词＋形容词”省略结构。
主动关系可用 doing 压缩，但非谓语逻辑主语必须与主句主语一致。
被动关系可用 done 压缩；when/if/although 等连词可保留以明确逻辑。

questions.question: When young, she lived abroad. 省略了什么？
questions.correct: 同主语且含 be，可省略 she was。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：同主语且含 be，可省略 she was。

questions.question: If necessary 最接近什么？
questions.correct: 这是固定省略结构。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：这是固定省略结构。

questions.question: Walking home, I met Mia. 中谁在 walking？
questions.correct: 分词逻辑主语与主句主语一致。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：分词逻辑主语与主句主语一致。

questions.question: Although ___, he did not attend. 表示“虽然被邀请”。
questions.correct: he 承受 invite，使用 done。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：he 承受 invite，使用 done。

narration.text:
状语从句可以变短，但前提是缩短后，谁在做动作仍然清楚。先看 When (she was) young, she lived abroad。<#0.7#>括号里的内容补出了完整结构。因为从句主语和主句主语相同，而且从句里有 be 动词，英语可以省掉从句主语和 be，只留下表示年轻状态的部分。If necessary 也是常见短式，相当于“如果有必要”。
再看 Walking home, I met Mia。walking 的动作虽然没有写主语，但逻辑上必须由主句主语 I 来完成，也就是“我走回家时遇见了米娅”。如果让读者误以为 Mia 在走，省略就失败了。<#0.8#>
最后看 Although invited, he did not attend。he 是被邀请的人，所以用过去分词 invited 表被动；保留 although，让“虽然被邀请但没参加”的让步关系清楚。判断能否省略时依次检查：从句和主句是不是同一个主语；是主动动作还是承受动作；连接词删掉后逻辑会不会模糊。同主语且含 be，可省主语和 be；主动常用 doing，被动常用 done，但不能只为句子短就强行转换。

lessons.title: 状语从句综合逻辑辨析
lessons.meta: 根据真实逻辑选择连接词，而非只看中文词面
examples: Because the road was closed, we took another route.
Although the road was closed, the race continued.
If the road is closed, we will take another route.
When the road is closed, traffic moves slowly.

exampleNotes.title: 逻辑关系
exampleNotes.body: 道路关闭是改道的真实原因，不是时间或让步。

exampleNotes.title: 易混辨析
exampleNotes.body: 同一事实若与主句形成反预期关系，应选择让步连接词。

exampleNotes.title: 易混辨析
exampleNotes.body: 道路是否关闭尚未确定，只是假设条件。

exampleNotes.title: 易混辨析
exampleNotes.body: 这里表示每逢道路关闭时出现的规律性结果。

rules: 原因从句陈述主句事件发生的理由或依据。
让步从句提供本应阻碍主句但未能阻碍的事实。
条件从句提出尚待满足或假设的前提。
时间从句定位事件发生时间，也可表达反复出现的时间规律。

questions.question: 道路关闭导致改道，应选择什么？
questions.correct: 这是直接原因。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：这是直接原因。

questions.question: 道路关闭但比赛仍继续，应选择什么？
questions.correct: 结果反预期，是让步。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：结果反预期，是让步。

questions.question: 道路可能关闭，若关闭就改道，应选择什么？
questions.correct: 这是未确定的条件。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：这是未确定的条件。

questions.question: 每逢道路关闭，交通都变慢，应选择什么？
questions.correct: when 表示反复发生的时间情境。
questions.wrong: 再看逻辑：when 表示反复发生的时间情境。

narration.text:
同一个事实放进不同连接词，主句和它的关系会完全改变。这一节不要先找中文对应词，而要问说话人想表达哪种逻辑。先看 Because the road was closed, we took another route。<#0.7#>道路关闭已经发生，并且直接导致改道，所以是原因。because 回答“为什么换路线”。
Although the road was closed, the race continued 仍然承认道路关闭这个事实，但正常预期是比赛难以继续，实际却继续了，因此是让步。If the road is closed, we will take another route 又不同：道路是否关闭还没确定，只把它当成改道的条件。<#0.8#>
最后看 When the road is closed, traffic moves slowly。这里不是说某一次原因，而是描述一种反复出现的时间情境：每逢道路关闭，交通就变慢。四句都围绕道路关闭，连接词却分别让它成为原因、阻碍仍未改变结果、尚待满足的条件，或反复发生的时间背景。判断顺序是：事实是否直接导致结果？本应阻碍却仍发生？事情是否尚未确定？还是在说每逢某时的规律？按真实关系选择对应连接词。

en.title: Adverbial clauses · 20 lessons
en.copy: Build a complete logic system of time, place, reason, purpose, result, condition, concession, comparison and manner.

course.title: Definition, core and boundary of adverbial clauses
course.meta: The whole clause adds time, reason, condition and other relations to the main clause
examples: When the bell rang, the students left.
Because the road was closed, we turned back.
The students left when the bell rang.
Because of the rain, we stayed inside.

analyses.label: Time adverbial clause: when links it to the main clause
Reason adverbial clause: because marks the cause
Prepositional phrase as reason adverbial, not a clause

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: First find the main skeleton the students left. When the bell rang has its own the bell + rang skeleton, but as a whole it only answers when the students left.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The main skeleton is we turned back. Because the road was closed fills no subject or object slot; it explains why the turning back happened.

exampleNotes.title: Position and punctuation
exampleNotes.body: The final time clause is tightly integrated with left, so it normally takes no comma. Both languages can understand it as the time of leaving without a mechanical reordering rule.

exampleNotes.title: Boundary note
exampleNotes.body: Because of the rain also gives a reason, but the rain has no predicate, so it is a prepositional phrase. An adverbial clause must contain its own subject-predicate skeleton.

rules: An adverbial clause has its own inner subject-predicate skeleton but functions as one outer adverbial, adding time, place, reason or another relation to the main event.
A connector does more than join two clauses: it identifies the specific logical relation between the subordinate and main clauses.
An initial adverbial clause is normally separated by a comma; a tightly integrated final clause normally is not.
To identify a clause, check for an inner subject-predicate skeleton. A prepositional phrase such as because of may also be adverbial, but it is not a clause.

questions.question: What does the When-clause function as a whole?
questions.correct: It has an inner skeleton and externally gives the time of left.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: It has an inner skeleton and externally gives the time of left.

questions.question: What does because mark in this sentence?
questions.correct: The road closure explains why they turned back.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The road closure explains why they turned back.

questions.question: How is the tightly integrated final clause normally punctuated?
questions.correct: The final time clause is tightly integrated with left.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The final time clause is tightly integrated with left.

questions.question: Why is Because of the rain not an adverbial clause?

options.text: It has no inner subject-predicate skeleton

questions.correct: the rain is the prepositional object and there is no inner predicate.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: the rain is the prepositional object and there is no inner predicate.

narration.text:
先看 When the bell rang, the students left。<#0.7#>真正要说的主干是 the students left，也就是“学生离开了”。When the bell rang 里面也有自己的主语 the bell 和动作 rang，但它整个放在主干旁边，只负责回答“什么时候离开”。这就是状语从句：里面是一套小句子，放到外面却像一个时间、原因或条件说明。
第二句 Because the road was closed, we turned back。主干换成 we turned back，前面的小句子回答“为什么返回”。所以连接词不能只当成开头标记；when 让两个事件形成时间关系，because 让它们形成原因关系，连接词一换，听者理解的关系也会跟着变。<#0.8#>
再看 The students left when the bell rang。时间从句放在后面，紧跟 left，通常不用逗号；放在前面时，逗号帮助我们看出背景讲完了，主句开始了。最后比较 Because of the rain, we stayed inside。the rain 只有名词，没有自己的谓语，因此 Because of the rain 是介词短语，不是从句。判断时先抓主句，再看附加部分有没有自己的主谓，最后问它给主句补的是哪一种关系。

course.title: Time: when, while and as
course.meta: Point, duration and simultaneous development
examples: When the phone rang, I answered it.
While I was studying, my brother was sleeping.
As the sun rose, the sky grew brighter.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: when can introduce an event at a particular point.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: while emphasizes overlapping durative actions.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: as commonly presents two processes developing together.

rules: when can refer to a point or period and has the broadest time use.
while commonly emphasizes overlap between durative actions or states.
as commonly means as/while, showing simultaneous actions or development.

questions.question: ___ the phone rang, I answered it.
questions.correct: Use when for the point event.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use when for the point event.

questions.question: ___ I was studying, my brother was sleeping.
questions.correct: while shows overlapping durative actions.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: while shows overlapping durative actions.

questions.question: ___ the sun rose, the sky grew brighter, emphasizing simultaneous change.
questions.correct: as can mean as the process develops.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: as can mean as the process develops.

narration.text:
when、while 和 as 都能说“当……时”，但它们让我们看到的时间画面不一样。先看 When the phone rang, I answered it。<#0.7#>电话响是一个清楚的时间点，回答电话紧接着发生。这里用 when，重点是把 answered 定位在电话响起的那个时刻。when 的范围最宽，既能接时间点，也能接一段时间。
再看 While I was studying, my brother was sleeping。was studying 和 was sleeping 都在持续，两个动作有一段时间重叠。while 像是把一段时间框出来，让我们同时看到“我在学习”和“弟弟在睡觉”。如果只想抓某个突然发生的点，就不必强行用 while。<#0.8#>
最后看 As the sun rose, the sky grew brighter。太阳升起不是一下完成，天空变亮也在逐渐发生，两个变化一起往前走。as 在这里更接近“随着”。所以选择时不要只背中文翻译：要看画面。抓一个时刻，when 最自然；突出两个持续过程重叠，用 while；强调两个过程同步变化，用 as。先判断事件是一个点、一段重叠，还是一起发展，再选连接词。

course.title: Time: before and after
course.meta: Making event order explicit
examples: Wash your hands before you eat.
After she finished the report, she sent it.
After she had finished the report, she sent it.

analyses.text: After she had finished the report,
analyses.label: after-clause with past perfect

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The main action occurs before the subordinate action.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The subordinate event finishes first and the main event follows.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: When after already makes order clear, past perfect may emphasize prior completion but is not always required.

rules: A before-clause presents an event later than the main event.
An after-clause presents an event earlier than the main event.
When before/after makes order clear, simple past or past perfect may be chosen according to emphasis and context.

questions.question: Wash your hands ___ you eat.
questions.correct: Washing comes before eating.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Washing comes before eating.

questions.question: ___ she finished the report, she sent it.
questions.correct: Finishing precedes sending.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Finishing precedes sending.

questions.question: Which form emphasizes earlier completion?
questions.correct: Past perfect emphasizes completion before sent.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Past perfect emphasizes completion before sent.

narration.text:
before 和 after 的核心不是翻译，而是给两个动作排队。先看 Wash your hands before you eat。<#0.7#>主句要求先洗手，before you eat 把“吃饭”放到后面，所以顺序是洗手在前，吃饭在后。看到 before 时，可以把从句里的动作当成一个时间界线，主句动作发生在这条界线之前。
第二句 After she finished the report, she sent it。after 从句放在前面，告诉我们报告先完成，随后才发送。不要因为从句写在句首，就误以为句首动作一定晚发生；真正决定先后的，是 after 的意义。<#0.8#>
再看 After she had finished the report, she sent it。had finished 用过去完成时，把“先完成”再突出一次。但 after 本身已经把顺序说清，所以很多语境里 finished 就足够，过去完成时不是见到 after 就必须使用。判断时先圈出两个事件，再让连接词排顺序：before 后的事件较晚，after 后的事件较早。时态负责补充强调，连接词才是判断时最先要看的路标。

course.title: Time: until and since
course.meta: Endpoint and starting point
examples: We waited until the bus arrived.
She did not leave until the meeting ended.
I have lived here since I graduated.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The waiting continues up to the bus arrival endpoint.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: not ... until means the main action begins only at the endpoint.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: The since-clause gives a past starting point; present perfect commonly shows continuation to now.

rules: In an affirmative clause, a durative action may continue until the stated endpoint.
not ... until means the main action does not happen before the stated time.
A since-clause marks a starting point; the main clause commonly uses a perfect tense and the since-clause simple past.

questions.question: We waited ___ the bus arrived.
questions.correct: The waiting lasts to the arrival.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The waiting lasts to the arrival.

questions.question: She did not leave ___ the meeting ended.
questions.correct: not until means she left only when it ended.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: not until means she left only when it ended.

questions.question: I ___ here since I graduated.
questions.correct: Use present perfect for continuation from a past point to now.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use present perfect for continuation from a past point to now.

narration.text:
until 和 since 都在时间线上找一个点，但一个看终点，一个看起点。先看 We waited until the bus arrived。<#0.7#>waited 是持续动作，等待一直延续，直到公交车到达才结束。until the bus arrived 就像给等待画出右边的终点，重点不是公交到达持续多久，而是等待到哪里停止。
第二句 She did not leave until the meeting ended。这里不能机械理解成“离开一直持续”。did not leave 表示之前始终没有离开，会议结束时，leave 这个动作才发生。not ... until 常表达“直到……才……”。<#0.8#>
再看 I have lived here since I graduated。since I graduated 给出过去的起点，have lived 表示从毕业以后一直延续到现在。于是常见组合是：since 从句用一般过去时交代起点，主句用现在完成时连接过去和现在。判断时先问动作是在某一点结束，还是从某一点开始。看到终点用 until；看到起点并延续到现在，用 since 和完成时。特别注意 not until，它说的是动作到终点才开始，不是普通的“持续到”。

course.title: Time: as soon as and once
course.meta: Immediate sequence and once a condition is met
examples: Call me as soon as you arrive.
Once you understand the rule, the task becomes easier.
I will tell you as soon as I know.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The main action follows immediately when the subordinate event occurs.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: once means once, combining time sequence with a condition being met.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: The main clause uses will; the future-time clause uses present simple know.

rules: as soon as shows one event following immediately after another.
once means once and often combines temporal and conditional meaning.
For future reference, as soon as/once clauses normally use present simple, not will for plain futurity.

questions.question: Call me ___ you arrive.
questions.correct: It means call immediately upon arrival.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: It means call immediately upon arrival.

questions.question: ___ you understand the rule, the task becomes easier.
questions.correct: once means once the condition is met.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: once means once the condition is met.

questions.question: I will tell you as soon as I ___.
questions.correct: Use present simple in the future-time clause.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use present simple in the future-time clause.

narration.text:
as soon as 和 once 都把两个事件接得很近，但重点略有不同。先看 Call me as soon as you arrive。<#0.7#>arrive 一发生，call 就要紧接着发生，中间不希望有明显等待。as soon as 强调“一……就……”，适合表达立即跟上的动作。
第二句 Once you understand the rule, the task becomes easier。这里 once 不只是说时间先后，还带有“条件一旦成立”的感觉：只要理解规则，任务就会变容易。所以 once 经常站在时间和条件的交界处。<#0.8#>
最后看 I will tell you as soon as I know。主句 will tell 明确指向将来，从句虽然也说将来的“知道”，却用一般现在时 know，不说 will know。原因是这个连接语已经把它放进未来时间安排里，不需要再用普通 will 重复标记。判断时先看你要表达的是“马上跟着发生”，还是“一旦条件成立”。前者使用表示“一……就……”的连接语，后者可用 once。谈将来时，再检查从句是否误加了 will。

course.title: Place: where and wherever
course.meta: Where and wherever
examples: Stay where you are.
Where there is water, life can exist.
Wherever you go, I will follow you.

exampleNotes.title: Word-order translation
exampleNotes.body: where you are means in the place where you are and modifies stay.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The clause generalizes over places where water exists.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: wherever means no matter where, with unrestricted place.

rules: A where place clause gives the location of the main action.
An initial where-clause may generalize as in places where, followed by the main result.
wherever expresses any place or no matter where and is less restricted than where.

questions.question: Stay ___ you are.
questions.correct: The clause gives the location of stay.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The clause gives the location of stay.

questions.question: ___ there is water, life can exist.
questions.correct: It means in places where water exists.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: It means in places where water exists.

questions.question: ___ you go, I will follow you.
questions.correct: wherever means no matter where.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: wherever means no matter where.

narration.text:
地点状语从句不是单独说一个地点名，而是用一整套主谓关系回答“在哪里”。先看 Stay where you are。<#0.7#>主干只有 Stay，也就是“待着”。where you are 里面有 you 和 are，整个小句子说明 stay 的地点：待在你现在所在的位置。它不是 stay 的宾语，而是给动作补地点范围。
再看 Where there is water, life can exist。where there is water 概括的不是某一个已知地点，而是所有“有水的地方”；主句说这些地方可能有生命。句首地点从句先搭好一个空间背景，后面的结论在这个范围内成立。<#0.8#>
最后看 Wherever you go, I will follow you。wherever 比 where 更开放，意思是无论你去哪个地方，主句结果都不改变。选择时先问范围是否有限：只是指出动作发生的地方，用 where；想把所有可能地点都包括进去，用 wherever。判断地点从句时仍要检查内部主谓；这三个地点从句都有自己的主语和谓语，有了这套骨架，它才是从句，而不只是一个地点词。

course.title: Reason: because, since and as
course.meta: Direct reason and shared background
examples: We stayed inside because it was raining.
Since everyone is here, we can begin.
As it was getting late, we went home.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: because directly answers why and strongly focuses the reason.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: since often presents a known or readily accepted reason as background.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: An as-reason clause is often initial and backgrounded.

rules: because expresses a direct focused reason and naturally answers why.
Causal since commonly presents a known, obvious or assumed reason.
Causal as is usually weaker and often supplies initial background.

questions.question: Why did you stay inside? — ___ it was raining.
questions.correct: because directly answers why.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: because directly answers why.

questions.question: ___ everyone is here, we can begin, presenting a shared premise.
questions.correct: since supplies a known reason.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: since supplies a known reason.

questions.question: ___ it was getting late, we went home, giving a background reason.
questions.correct: as presents a backgrounded reason.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: as presents a backgrounded reason.

narration.text:
because、since 和 as 都能给原因，但说话人把原因放在多重要的位置，并不一样。先看 We stayed inside because it was raining。<#0.7#>如果别人问“为什么待在里面”，because it was raining 就是直接答案。because 把下雨作为重点原因，解释力度最清楚。
第二句 Since everyone is here, we can begin。everyone is here 更像双方都看得到、都能接受的前提。说话人不是重点追问原因，而是借这个已知背景推出“可以开始”。since 在这里接近“既然”。<#0.8#>
再看 As it was getting late, we went home。天色渐晚被轻轻放在句首当背景，真正要推进的信息是 we went home。as 表原因时通常比 because 弱，也常前置。选择时不要把三个词当成随意替换：需要正面回答 why，用 because；原因已经明显，拿来作为推理前提，用 since；只是顺带铺一个较弱背景，可用 as。先判断原因是不是句子的焦点，再决定连接词。

course.title: Purpose: so that and in order that
course.meta: So that an intended outcome can happen
examples: Speak slowly so that everyone can understand.
She left early so that she could catch the bus.
In order that no one would notice, he entered quietly.
He spoke so quietly that nobody heard him.

analyses.label: Past-context purpose clause

analyses.text: In order that no one would notice,
analyses.label: Formal purpose clause

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The clause gives the purpose of speaking slowly and commonly contains can/may.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: Past contexts commonly use could/might/would for the intended result.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: in order that is more formal, explicitly marks purpose and can be initial.

exampleNotes.title: Contrast
exampleNotes.body: Here so + adverb quietly + that gives the actual result that nobody heard him; it is not purpose so that introducing an intention.

rules: Purpose so that commonly combines with can/could, may/might or will/would.
With a past main context, a purpose clause commonly uses could, might or would.
in order that is more formal and explicit than so that and may be initial.
A purpose so that clause gives an intention; so + adjective/adverb + that gives the actual result of a degree.

questions.correct: The clause gives the purpose.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The clause gives the purpose.

questions.correct: Use could in the past context.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use could in the past context.

questions.wrong: Check the logic: in order that is the formal purpose connector.

questions.question: What does the that-clause express in this sentence?
questions.correct: The degree expressed by so quietly produced the result.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The degree expressed by so quietly produced the result.

narration.text:
目的从句说的是“做这件事，想让什么发生”，它描述意图，不保证结果真的实现。先看 Speak slowly so that everyone can understand。<#0.7#>主干是 Speak slowly，慢慢说的目标，是让每个人能够听懂。can understand 表示这种能力或可能性，因此 so that 后常见 can、may 一类情态词。
第二句 She left early so that she could catch the bus。主句在过去，目的从句用 could，表示她早走是为了能赶上公交。句子只交代她的打算，并没有保证最后一定赶上。in order that no one would notice, he entered quietly 也是目的，但 in order that 更正式，放在句首时，目的被先交代出来。<#0.8#>
最后比较 He spoke so quietly that nobody heard him。这里不是“为了没人听见”，而是声音安静到实际造成没人听见。结构是 so quietly 加 that，quietly 的程度带来结果。判断目的还是结果，可以问：这是行动前想达到的目标，还是行动后已经出现的后果？目标用普通或更正式的目的连接结构；程度造成的实际后果，用 so 加形容词或副词再接 that。

course.title: Result: so...that and such...that
course.meta: A degree leading to a result
examples: The box was so heavy that I could not lift it.
It was such a difficult question that nobody answered it.
There were so many people that we could not enter.

analyses.text: that I could not lift it.
analyses.label: Result adverbial clause

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: so modifies the adjective heavy and the that-clause gives the result.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: such modifies an a + adjective + noun phrase.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: Use so before many/much/few/little.

rules: so + adjective/adverb + that expresses a degree producing a result.
such + (a/an) + adjective + noun + that expresses a thing or situation producing a result.
many, much, few and little as quantity words normally use so ... that.

questions.question: The box was ___ heavy that I could not lift it.
questions.correct: Use so before the adjective heavy.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use so before the adjective heavy.

questions.question: It was ___ difficult question that nobody answered it.
questions.correct: Use such a before the noun phrase.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use such a before the noun phrase.

questions.question: There were ___ many people that we could not enter.
questions.correct: Use so before many.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use so before many.

narration.text:
so...that 和 such...that 都在说“程度达到这里，于是出现那个结果”。区别先看 that 前面中心是什么。The box was so heavy that I could not lift it。<#0.7#>heavy 是形容词，so 直接把“重”的程度提高，that 从句说明实际结果：我抬不起来。结构可以先抓成 so heavy，再接结果。
第二句 It was such a difficult question that nobody answered it。这里中心是 question，是名词。such 带着整个 a difficult question，表示“这样一道难题”，随后出现无人回答的结果。不是看到 difficult 就只选 so，还要看它和 a、question 组成了完整名词短语。<#0.8#>
再看 There were so many people that we could not enter。many 虽然修饰 people，但 many、much、few、little 表数量时习惯放在 so 后面，所以是 so many people。选择时先看结构：形容词或副词直接表示程度，用 so；a 加形容词加名词这一整组，用 such；遇到数量词 many、much、few、little，优先用 so。that 后面说的都是真实造成的结果，不是行动目的。

course.title: Condition: if
course.meta: Real possibility, hypothesis and instructions
examples: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.
If you heat ice, it melts.
If you need help, call me.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: A future real condition uses present simple rains in the if-clause and may use will in the main clause.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: General truths commonly use present simple in both clauses.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The main clause may be imperative, giving an instruction if the condition holds.

rules: A real if-clause presents a possible condition and the main clause its result.
General truths may use present simple in both the if-clause and main clause.
The main clause of a condition need not use will; it may use another modal or an imperative.

questions.question: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay home.
questions.correct: Use present simple in the future condition.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use present simple in the future condition.

questions.question: If you heat ice, it ___.
questions.correct: A general truth can use present simple in both clauses.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: A general truth can use present simple in both clauses.

questions.question: If you need help, ___ me.
questions.correct: The main clause can be imperative.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The main clause can be imperative.

narration.text:
if 从句先提出一个前提，主句再说这个前提成立会怎样。先看 If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home。<#0.7#>下雨还没有发生，只是明天可能出现的条件。主句用 will stay 说结果，从句却用 rains，不用 will rain。一般现在时放在这里不表示“现在下雨”，而是英语表达将来条件的常见方式。
第二句 If you heat ice, it melts。这里不是预测某一次未来，而是在说反复成立的规律：只要给冰加热，它就融化。因此条件和结果都用一般现在时。<#0.8#>
再看 If you need help, call me。条件成立后，主句不是 will，而是祈使句 call me，直接给出建议或指令。这说明条件句的主句有多种样子，不必套成唯一公式。判断时分两步：先看条件是未来可能、普遍规律，还是给指令的前提；再选主句形式。未来真实条件常见“if 加一般现在时，主句用 will”；规律两边都用现在时；建议和命令可以直接用祈使句。

course.title: Condition: unless, as long as and provided that
course.meta: Unless, as long as and provided that
examples: Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
You may stay as long as you are quiet.
We will go provided that the weather is safe.

analyses.label: as-long-as condition clause

analyses.text: provided that the weather is safe.
analyses.label: provided-that condition clause

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: unless is equivalent to if ... not; the clause normally does not repeat not.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: as long as means provided that a condition continues to hold.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: provided/providing that explicitly means on condition that.

rules: unless means if ... not; except for special meanings, it normally does not repeat not.
Conditional as long as means provided that and should be distinguished from duration.
provided/providing that states an explicit condition and is relatively formal.

questions.question: ___ you hurry, you will miss the bus.
questions.correct: unless means if you do not hurry.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: unless means if you do not hurry.

questions.question: You may stay ___ you are quiet.
questions.correct: It means provided that you are quiet.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: It means provided that you are quiet.

questions.question: We will go ___ the weather is safe.
questions.correct: provided that states the condition.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: provided that states the condition.

narration.text:
三种连接方式都在设条件，但门槛的方向不同。先看 Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus。<#0.7#>unless you hurry 相当于“如果你不赶快”，也就是“不赶快的话”。unless 自己已经带有否定方向，通常不要再重复否定，否则意思可能变乱。
第二句 You may stay as long as you are quiet。这里 as long as 不是“和……一样长”，而是“只要”。安静这个条件持续满足，就可以留下。它强调许可建立在这个条件上。<#0.8#>
再看 We will go provided that the weather is safe。provided that 把前提说得很明确：只有天气安全，才会去，语气比普通 if 更正式。选择时先看你想怎样设门槛：第一种表达“如果不……就……”；第二种表达“只要条件保持成立”；第三种正式说明“前提是”。最后再检查第一种连接词后面是否不必要地重复了否定。

course.title: Concession: although, though and even though
course.meta: The main result holds despite the condition
examples: Although it was cold, we went out.
Though he was tired, he kept working.
Even though she knew the risk, she continued.
Even if it rains, we will go.

analyses.text: Even though she knew the risk,
analyses.label: even-though concessive clause

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The cold might prevent going out, yet the main result still occurs.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: though is often slightly less formal than although, with similar basic meaning.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: even though emphasizes a particularly unexpected contrast.

exampleNotes.title: Contrast
exampleNotes.body: even if treats rain as an unresolved possibility; even though it is raining would present it as a fact.

rules: although introduces factual concession, with a main result contrary to expectation.
though is close to although, often less formal and more positionally flexible.
even though emphasizes that the main result holds despite a strong factual obstacle.
even though introduces an accepted fact, whereas even if introduces a hypothetical or unresolved possibility.

questions.question: ___ it was cold, we went out.
questions.correct: The relation is concessive.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The relation is concessive.

questions.question: Which word is often slightly less formal than although?
questions.correct: though is similar but often less formal.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: though is similar but often less formal.

questions.question: Which marks stronger concession?
questions.correct: even strengthens the unexpected contrast.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: even strengthens the unexpected contrast.

questions.question: Rain is uncertain, but we will go regardless: ___ it rains, we will go.
questions.correct: Use even if for the unresolved possibility.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use even if for the unresolved possibility.

narration.text:
让步关系可以理解成：前面的情况本来可能阻止结果，可结果还是发生了。先看 Although it was cold, we went out。<#0.7#>天冷通常让人不想外出，但 we went out 仍然成立。although 不是原因，它专门提醒听者：后面的结果和通常预期不一样。
Though he was tired, he kept working 表达同样的转折预期，though 一般更口语、更灵活。Even though she knew the risk, she continued 里的 even 把阻碍再加强：她明明知道风险，仍然继续，反差更明显。<#0.8#>
最后看 Even if it rains, we will go。这里下雨还没确定，只是假设一个可能情况；无论是否发生，去这件事都不变。even though 引出的是已经承认的事实，even if 引出的是尚未确定的假设。判断时先找“本来会阻止什么”的因素，再看它是事实还是可能。普通事实让步用 although 或 though；想加强反差用 even though；情况尚未发生，只是假设也不改变结果，用 even if。

course.title: Concession: while, no matter and wh-ever
course.meta: Contrastive and unconditional concession
examples: While I understand your point, I disagree.

Wherever she goes, she makes friends.
Whoever calls, do not answer

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: Concessive while highlights contrast between two positions.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: Whatever happens, the main instruction holds.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: wherever equals no matter where here and expresses unconditional concession.

exampleNotes.title: Boundary note
exampleNotes.body: wh-ever is concessive here; no matter + wh- cannot replace nominal subject/object uses, which are outside this lesson.

rules: while can mark contrastive concession, commonly initially, meaning although.
no matter + wh- means the main result is unchanged under any alternative.
A wh-ever form can equal no matter + wh- in a concessive adverbial clause.
Classify wh-ever by the clause’s overall function; this lesson covers only concessive adverbial use.

questions.question: ___ I understand your point, I disagree, marking contrastive concession.
questions.correct: while can mean although.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: while can mean although.

questions.question: ___ what happens, stay calm.
questions.correct: no matter what expresses unconditional concession.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: no matter what expresses unconditional concession.

questions.question: What is closest to “Wherever she goes”?
questions.correct: wherever can equal no matter where.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: wherever can equal no matter where.

questions.question: What should be checked first to classify a wh-ever clause?

options.text: Its function in the whole sentence

questions.correct: The same form may serve different clause functions.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The same form may serve different clause functions.

narration.text:
这一节的让步不是简单说“但是”，而是说明无论出现哪一种情况，主句结论仍然不变。先看 While I understand your point, I disagree。<#0.7#>我理解你的观点，却仍不同意。while 在这里不表示两个动作同时发生，而是把“理解”和“不同意”放在一起形成对比，接近“虽然”。
No matter what happens, stay calm 把可能发生的所有事情都包括进来：不管发生什么，保持冷静这条指令不变。Wherever she goes, she makes friends 也是同样思路，wherever 表示“无论哪里”，不论地点怎样变化，结果都成立。<#0.8#>
最后看 Whoever calls, do not answer。不论打来电话的是谁，指令都不改变。判断 wh-ever 时不能只看到 ever 就下结论，要看整块内容在句中做什么。这些从句都给主句加“无论哪种情况”的让步范围。选择时，对比两个立场可用 while；想展开所有可能，用 no matter 加疑问词，或用 whatever、wherever、whoever 这样的形式。

course.title: Comparison: than and as...as
course.meta: Comparative difference and equality
examples: Mia runs faster than I do.
This room is as bright as that one is.
She is taller than me / than I am.

analyses.label: Comparison standard: than me is a phrase; than I am is a clause

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: than I do supplies the standard for faster; do substitutes for runs to avoid repeating the predicate.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: bright is the complement of room; the second as introduces that one is as the standard of equality.

exampleNotes.title: Contrast
exampleNotes.body: than me is common in everyday English; than I am overtly contains a subject and predicate, making it a full comparison clause and more formal.

rules: than introduces the comparison standard; repeated material is often replaced by an auxiliary or omitted.
as + adjective/adverb + as expresses equality, with the second as introducing a comparison clause.
After than, both an object-form phrase and a full nominative clause occur, with different formality.

questions.question: Mia runs faster than I ___.
questions.correct: do substitutes for runs.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: do substitutes for runs.

questions.question: This room is ___ bright ___ that one is.
questions.correct: Use as ... as for equality.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use as ... as for equality.

questions.correct: than I am overtly contains subject and predicate.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: than I am overtly contains subject and predicate.

narration.text:
比较从句的任务，是给比较词提供一个基准。先看 Mia runs faster than I do。<#0.7#>主干先说 Mia runs faster，但 faster 必须回答“比谁更快”。than I do 提供参照，do 代替前面已经出现的 runs，避免把相同的“跑”再完整说一遍。这个 do 不是新的动作意思，只是把相同谓语简洁地接住。
第二句 This room is as bright as that one is。第一个 as 和 bright 组成 as bright，表示达到同等亮度；第二个 as 引出比较对象 that one。后面的 is 对应前面的 is bright，重复的 bright 可以省掉。<#0.8#>
再看 She is taller than me / than I am。than me 在日常口语中很常见，可以看成较短的比较短语；than I am 明确写出主语和谓语，是完整比较从句，也更正式。判断时先找比较中心，是 faster、taller，还是 as bright；再找它跟谁比。比较从句里与前面重复的内容常被助动词代替或直接省略，所以不要因为句子短，就误认为结构不完整。

course.meta: Following a manner and presenting an apparent situation
examples: Do as I showed you.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: Present tense may leave the apparent situation open or plausible.

exampleNotes.title: Contrast
exampleNotes.body: Past knew can mark remoteness from current fact or speaker disbelief.

rules: as introduces a manner clause meaning in the way that.
as if/as though may use ordinary indicative tense when the appearance is potentially real.
Past forms or were after as if/as though can mark present unreality or remoteness.

questions.question: Do ___ I showed you.
questions.correct: as means in the way shown.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: as means in the way shown.

questions.question: What may follow as if when the situation seems plausibly real?
questions.correct: Indicative tense is possible for a plausible situation.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Indicative tense is possible for a plausible situation.

questions.question: He talks as if he ___ everything, implying disbelief.

questions.wrong: Check the logic: Past tense marks remoteness or unreality.

narration.text:
方式从句回答“动作是按照什么样子发生的”。先看 Do as I showed you。<#0.7#>主句只有 Do，真正的操作方式由 as I showed you 补出来，意思是按照我展示的方法做。as 在这里不是原因，也不是时间，要看它是否给动作提供一个可照着执行的样子。
第二句 He speaks as if he knows everything。说话的样子像是他什么都知道。knows 用一般现在时，说明说话人至少把这种可能性留着，并没有明确断定它不真实。<#0.8#>
再看 He talks as if he knew everything。同样是“仿佛”，knew 用过去式却不一定表示过去时间，它可以把情况推远，暗示说话人并不相信他真的什么都知道。选择时先分两类：明确表示“按照……方式”，用 as；表示外在样子“好像……”，用 as if 或 as though。然后再判断说话人态度：觉得可能真实，用普通时态；想表达与现实有距离或不相信，可用过去式，涉及 be 时也常见 were。

course.title: Future time and condition clauses use present forms
course.meta: The present-in-subordinate rule and its limits
examples: When she arrives, we will start.
If he calls, tell me.

I do not know whether he will come.
If you will wait here, I will check the schedule.

exampleNotes.body: arrives has future reference, but the clause does not use will arrive.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus

exampleNotes.title: Boundary note

exampleNotes.title: Boundary note
exampleNotes.body: will here does not merely predict the future; it means if you are willing to wait. The no-will rule is therefore not exceptionless.

rules: Future-time clauses with when, before, after, until or as soon as normally use present simple.
Real future condition clauses with if, unless or as long as normally use present simple.
Present perfect may emphasize completion in a future time or condition clause.
The present-in-subordinate rule applies to relevant time/condition adverbial clauses, not every object clause.
will is possible in an if-clause when it expresses willingness, insistence or a polite request rather than plain futurity.

questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use present simple in the future-time clause.

questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use present simple in the future condition.

questions.wrong: Check the logic: Present perfect adds emphasis that the subordinate action is complete.

questions.wrong: Check the logic: will can express future time in this present reporting context.

questions.wrong: Check the logic: will expresses willingness here, not plain future time.

narration.text:
“主将从现”不是看到两个分句就套用，而是专门处理将来的时间或真实条件。先看 When she arrives, we will start。<#0.7#>开始发生在将来，主句用 will start；when 已经把 arrives 放到未来时间里，所以从句用一般现在时。If he calls, tell me 也一样，calls 表示将来可能条件，主句则直接用祈使句。
Once you have finished, you may leave 使用现在完成时 have finished，重点是先把事情完成，再允许离开。它仍属于现在形式，不需要普通 will。<#0.8#>
但 I do not know whether he will come 不受这条规则限制，因为 whether he will come 是 do not know 的宾语，讨论的是“他是否会来”，不是条件状语从句，所以可以用 will。最后看 If you will wait here, I will check the schedule。从句里的 will 表“如果你愿意等”，说的是意愿，不是单纯预测。判断时先确认从句功能：是将来时间或真实条件，通常用现在形式；是宾语从句，或者 will 自己表达意愿，就不能机械删掉。

course.title: Tense relations in time clauses
course.meta: Simultaneity, interruption, sequence and duration
examples: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
When I arrived, they were eating.
By the time we arrived, the film had started.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: Past progressive gives the ongoing background; simple past gives the interrupting event.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: arrived is the point event; were eating is ongoing at that time.

exampleNotes.title: Tense focus
exampleNotes.body: The film started before arrival, so past perfect marks the earlier event.

rules: An ongoing background commonly uses past progressive and the interrupting short event simple past.
when can locate a point in time while a main progressive shows what was ongoing then.
by the time emphasizes an endpoint; an earlier completed past action commonly uses past perfect.

questions.question: While I ___, the phone rang.
questions.correct: Use past progressive for the ongoing background.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Use past progressive for the ongoing background.

questions.question: When I arrived, they ___.
questions.correct: It means eating was in progress at arrival.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: It means eating was in progress at arrival.

questions.correct: Past perfect explicitly marks the film’s start as earlier than arrival.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Past perfect explicitly marks the film’s start as earlier than arrival.

narration.text:
时间从句里的时态，是在帮我们看清两个过去动作怎样摆放：谁在持续，谁突然发生，谁更早完成。先看 While I was cooking, the phone rang。<#0.7#>was cooking 拉出一段持续背景，rang 是在这段背景中突然出现的短动作。可以想成一条长线被一个点打断，所以背景用过去进行时，点状事件用一般过去时。
第二句 When I arrived, they were eating。arrived 是到达的时间点，were eating 表示在那个时刻，吃饭正在进行。它和第一句的画面方向相反：时间点放在从句，持续背景放在主句，但判断方法相同。<#0.8#>
再看 By the time we arrived, the film had started。到达是截止点，电影开始发生得更早。had started 用过去完成时把“早于另一个过去动作”标出来。选择时不要只看到 while 就一定用进行时，而要看动作本身是否持续；也不要见到两个过去动作就都用过去完成时。先画时间线：持续背景用过去进行时，短动作常用一般过去时，需要突出在另一个过去点之前已经完成，才用过去完成时。

course.title: The because–so and although–but boundary
course.meta: Do not duplicate subordination and coordination
examples: Because it rained, we stayed home.
It rained, so we stayed home.
Although she was tired, she continued.

exampleNotes.title: Boundary note
exampleNotes.body: In a standard sentence, because already subordinates the reason clause, so the main clause does not add so.

exampleNotes.title: Contrast
exampleNotes.body: Alternatively so may coordinate the clauses, but then because is not used.

exampleNotes.title: Boundary note
exampleNotes.body: although already marks concession, so standard structure does not add but before the main clause.

rules: Standard English normally does not use because ... so ... together for the same cause-result pair.
Choose either because-subordination or so-coordination according to information focus.
Standard English normally does not combine although/though ... but ... for the same concession.

questions.question: Because it rained, ___ we stayed home.
questions.correct: because already marks the relation.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: because already marks the relation.

questions.question: It rained, ___ we stayed home.
questions.correct: The first clause is the cause and the second the result, so use coordinating so.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The first clause is the cause and the second the result, so use coordinating so.

questions.question: Although she was tired, ___ she continued.
questions.correct: although already marks concession.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: although already marks concession.

narration.text:
中文里常说“因为……所以……”“虽然……但是……”，英语标准句子通常只选一套连接方式。先看 Because it rained, we stayed home。<#0.7#>because 已经把 it rained 变成原因背景，后面的 we stayed home 是主句，中间不需要再加 so。不是少翻了“所以”，而是英语已经用 because 把关系交代完成。
第二句 It rained, so we stayed home 也正确，但结构变了。这里没有 because，so 把“下雨”和“待在家”两个分句并列起来，明确后一句是结果。你可以突出原因从属关系，也可以用 so 推出结果，但不要两边同时占用。<#0.8#>
Although she was tired, she continued 同样如此。although 已经表示“疲惫本应阻碍继续，但结果仍发生”，主句前不再加 but。判断时先圈出已有连接词：用了 because，就直接接主句；用了 although 或 though，也直接接主句。想用 so 或 but，就拿掉前面的从属连词，重新组织成并列分句。英语不是漏掉一半，而是每个关系只让一套结构负责。

course.title: Ellipsis and participle reduction in adverbial clauses
course.meta: Same subject, omitted be, and active/passive relations
examples: When (she was) young, she lived abroad.
If necessary, call me.
Walking home, I met Mia.
Although invited, he did not attend.

analyses.label: Time clause with subject and be omitted

exampleNotes.title: Transformation
exampleNotes.body: When subjects match and the subordinate predicate contains be, the subject and be may be omitted.

exampleNotes.title: Transformation
exampleNotes.body: If necessary corresponds to If it is necessary and is a conventional reduction.

exampleNotes.title: Transformation
exampleNotes.body: It can correspond to While I was walking home; the logical subject must be I.

exampleNotes.title: Transformation
exampleNotes.body: he receives invite; retaining although makes concession explicit.

rules: When the subordinate and main subjects match and the subordinate clause contains be, the subject and be may often be omitted.
if necessary/possible and similar forms are common conjunction + adjective reductions.
An active relation may reduce to doing, but its logical subject must match the main subject.
A passive relation may reduce to done; a connector such as when, if or although may remain to clarify the relation.

questions.question: What is omitted in “When young, she lived abroad”?
questions.correct: Same subject plus be allows omission of she was.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: Same subject plus be allows omission of she was.

questions.question: What is closest to “If necessary”?
questions.correct: It is a conventional reduction.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: It is a conventional reduction.

questions.question: Who is walking?
questions.correct: The participle’s logical subject matches I.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The participle’s logical subject matches I.

questions.question: Although ___, he did not attend, meaning despite being invited.
questions.correct: he receives invite, so use done.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: he receives invite, so use done.

narration.text:
状语从句可以变短，但前提是缩短后，谁在做动作仍然清楚。先看 When (she was) young, she lived abroad。<#0.7#>括号里的内容补出了完整结构。因为从句主语和主句主语相同，而且从句里有 be 动词，英语可以省掉从句主语和 be，只留下表示年轻状态的部分。If necessary 也是常见短式，相当于“如果有必要”。
再看 Walking home, I met Mia。walking 的动作虽然没有写主语，但逻辑上必须由主句主语 I 来完成，也就是“我走回家时遇见了米娅”。如果让读者误以为 Mia 在走，省略就失败了。<#0.8#>
最后看 Although invited, he did not attend。he 是被邀请的人，所以用过去分词 invited 表被动；保留 although，让“虽然被邀请但没参加”的让步关系清楚。判断能否省略时依次检查：从句和主句是不是同一个主语；是主动动作还是承受动作；连接词删掉后逻辑会不会模糊。同主语且含 be，可省主语和 be；主动常用 doing，被动常用 done，但不能只为句子短就强行转换。

course.title: Integrated adverbial-clause logic
course.meta: Choose connectors from the actual logic, not a surface translation
examples: Because the road was closed, we took another route.
Although the road was closed, the race continued.
If the road is closed, we will take another route.
When the road is closed, traffic moves slowly.

exampleNotes.title: Logical relation
exampleNotes.body: The closure is the actual reason for taking another route, not time or concession.

exampleNotes.title: Contrast
exampleNotes.body: The same fact calls for concession when the main result is contrary to expectation.

exampleNotes.title: Contrast
exampleNotes.body: Whether the road is closed is unresolved; it is a condition.

exampleNotes.title: Contrast
exampleNotes.body: This gives a regular result whenever the road is closed.

rules: A reason clause gives the cause or basis of the main event.
A concessive clause gives a fact expected to prevent the main result but failing to do so.
A condition clause presents a pending or hypothetical requirement.
A time clause locates an event and may also express a recurring temporal pattern.

questions.question: Which relation fits when road closure causes a route change?
questions.correct: It is a direct reason.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: It is a direct reason.

questions.question: Which relation fits when the road is closed but the race continues?
questions.correct: The unexpected result calls for concession.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: The unexpected result calls for concession.

questions.question: Which relation fits a possible closure leading to a route change?
questions.correct: It is an unresolved condition.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: It is an unresolved condition.

questions.question: Which relation fits a recurring time pattern?
questions.correct: when expresses the recurring temporal situation.
questions.wrong: Check the logic: when expresses the recurring temporal situation.

narration.text:
同一个事实放进不同连接词，主句和它的关系会完全改变。这一节不要先找中文对应词，而要问说话人想表达哪种逻辑。先看 Because the road was closed, we took another route。<#0.7#>道路关闭已经发生，并且直接导致改道，所以是原因。because 回答“为什么换路线”。
Although the road was closed, the race continued 仍然承认道路关闭这个事实，但正常预期是比赛难以继续，实际却继续了，因此是让步。If the road is closed, we will take another route 又不同：道路是否关闭还没确定，只把它当成改道的条件。<#0.8#>
最后看 When the road is closed, traffic moves slowly。这里不是说某一次原因，而是描述一种反复出现的时间情境：每逢道路关闭，交通就变慢。四句都围绕道路关闭，连接词却分别让它成为原因、阻碍仍未改变结果、尚待满足的条件，或反复发生的时间背景。判断顺序是：事实是否直接导致结果？本应阻碍却仍发生？事情是否尚未确定？还是在说每逢某时的规律？按真实关系选择对应连接词。
